sections.html:
A quick West Allis sale starts with a decision about the buyer: someone using a mortgage, someone you find yourself, or a buyer paying cash. Each one meets the same three Wisconsin requirements. Namely a condition report for the buyer, an electronic transfer return for the state and a deed on record with Milwaukee County. Taking a mortgage out of the picture drops the loan and appraisal steps, which is where most listings lose weeks.

West Allis sits in Milwaukee County. The 2025 population estimate is 60,119, a touch under the 60,325 counted in 2020, across 11.38 square miles of land.

The city is dense, with modestly priced homes and a lot of renters. Roughly 55.5 percent of homes have their owners living in them, and the median value is $203,800. Your house competes with plenty of rental stock, so condition and presentation carry weight.

The 2020 census counted 29,015 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. Interstates 94 and 41/894 cross the city, so commute questions are common. Planning a December listing? Candy Cane Lane, on Oklahoma and Montana Avenues between 92nd and 96th Streets, draws heavy traffic on holiday nights, which can complicate showings on those blocks.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin law asks of you
sections.html:
A seller of a building with up to four units owes the buyer a finished real estate condition report, delivered inside 10 days of the contract being accepted. Under chapter 709, a buyer who is left empty-handed can cancel during the following two business days and take deposits back. Personal representatives, trustees and conservators who never lived in the house may skip the form, and so may sellers whose transfers the fee statute exempts.

The state also charges the grantor a transfer fee, set by s. 77.22 at 30 cents on each $100 of value. The seller pays it when the deed goes on record. Wis. Stat. 77.24 divides the money, 20 percent to the county and the balance to the state. Exemptions appear in s. 77.25. The list includes inheritances, certain parent-to-child transfers for nominal consideration, and a foreclosure deed given to the mortgage holder.

Your deed will be recorded downtown at 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds. Each document costs $30, and every conveyance needs the electronic transfer return receipt attached. No cards here: cash, a check or a money order only.

Recording usually takes three to five business days, in filing order, and the original is mailed back one to two weeks afterward. Trouble with the electronic return? The Wisconsin Department of Revenue answers at (608) 266-1594. The register's counter will not draft papers or advise you on the law, so a title company or attorney steps in. Questions about a pending recording go to (414) 278-4005.

sections.h2: Property taxes and back taxes in West Allis
sections.html:
West Allis taxes are billed by the city. Ahead of listing, phone the City Treasurer about due dates and installments, and the City Assessor about your assessed value and property record. Assessors in Wisconsin value a property at what it would fetch in a private sale, and the title company splits the current-year bill when you close.

The Milwaukee County Treasurer handles delinquent taxes for 2024 and earlier. That office serves every municipality in the county but the City of Milwaukee, and West Allis falls inside its coverage. State law attaches a delinquency charge of 18 percent a year, which makes early payment worthwhile. A call to (414) 278-4033 starts a payment plan. Paying online costs a 2.55 percent card fee or a $1.50 e-check fee, kept by the processor.

Owe back taxes? Ask the Treasurer for a payoff before you agree to anything, so the net you compare is accurate. Your closing agent can pay off the balance from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a West Allis owner?
sections.html:
Collect written terms from each buyer, then put the options next to one another.

  • Agent listing. Fits a house in presentable condition when you are not rushed.
  • For sale by owner. Keeps more of the price in your pocket but leaves disclosures and negotiations to you.
  • Cash buyer. Fits houses that need repairs, inherited or tenant-occupied properties, and owners trying to avoid foreclosure. Compare the net figure after title and recording costs.

Gather what a West Allis buyer will ask for before you list. Start one folder: the vesting deed, a current mortgage statement, the newest tax bill and repair records. The assessor's property record is worth printing, since it shows your assessed value and the details the city holds on the house.

A house from an estate needs documents proving who may sign the deed. If foreclosure is a worry, speak to a title company early. A sale can still close when the numbers work, and a cash offer can move on a date you pick.

sections.h2: Weighing offers against what you keep
sections.html:
Price alone can mislead. In a city this built-up, no buyer is short of choices, so the terms you can offer matter. A listing offer that depends on a buyer's loan may fall through at the appraisal, and a lower cash offer may close sooner and cost you less while you wait. For each offer, subtract the transfer fee, any tax balance, repairs the buyer wants and the months of upkeep before closing.

Find out who pays for title work and recording, and have that written into the offer. For an owner who has fallen behind, a firm closing date can beat a slightly higher price, so ask each buyer how fast they can close once title is clear.

sections.h2: Questions to put to your title company
sections.html:
A West Allis sale involves a few figures that only your closing agent can pin down. Ask how much will be needed to pay off your mortgage, and whether any tax balance has to be cleared at the same time. Ask how the current-year tax bill will be divided with the buyer, and which documents the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds will need with the deed.

Ask, too, who will file the electronic transfer return and when, because the register will not take a deed without it. Getting each answer in writing before closing day keeps surprises off the settlement statement.

When you accept an offer, the report clock starts, so complete the form right away. While that happens, the title company searches the records and prepares the deed and the return. On closing day you sign the deed, cover the transfer fee and settle any mortgage or tax balance from proceeds. The register's office then records the deed. With cash, the steps are the same minus the lender appraisal, and title work and recording decide the date.

faqs.q: How quickly can a West Allis house sell?
faqs.a: It turns on the buyer. A buyer who needs no loan skips approval and appraisal, which leaves the date to title work and recording. Financing brings showings, inspections and underwriting.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: Each document is $30, and the transfer fee on your return receipt is added. Pay by cash, check or money order, because cards are refused.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property taxes in West Allis?
faqs.a: The Milwaukee County Treasurer does, for 2024 and earlier years, across the county apart from the City of Milwaukee. The delinquency charge set by state law is 18 percent a year. Call (414) 278-4033 about a payment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not if you are a personal representative or trustee who never lived there, since Chapter 709 excuses those fiduciaries. Under s. 77.25 a transfer by will, descent or survivorship also avoids the transfer fee.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a West Allis sale?
faqs.a: The grantor pays it at recording, at 30 cents for every $100 of value. The electronic return goes to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.
